name: Smoldering (Asymptomatic) Myeloma: Active Surveillance (with high-risk systemic-therapy options)

biomarkers.note: Risk is stratified by the Mayo 2018 / IMWG 20/2/20 criteria (serum M-protein >2 g/dL, involved:uninvolved serum free light-chain ratio >20, bone marrow plasma cells >20 percent). High-risk features (and rising parameters over time) drive the decision to consider early therapy versus observation; there is no biomarker that mandates cytotoxic therapy in smoldering disease. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Multiple Myeloma, v5.2026, MYEL-3 and MS.

treatmentSetting: active surveillance (observation) is the primary management for smoldering myeloma; systemic therapy is reserved for select high-risk patients, ideally on a clinical trial
lineOfTherapy: primary management of smoldering (asymptomatic) myeloma; no cytotoxic therapy for standard-risk disease. Progression to symptomatic myeloma redirects to active-myeloma protocols

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: smoldering (asymptomatic) myeloma without myeloma-defining events (no CRAB features, no SLiM biomarkers)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v5.2026, MYEL-A (Definitions of Myeloma and Related Plasma-Cell Disorders); MYEL-3 (Smoldering Myeloma)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: stratify by Mayo 2018 / IMWG 20/2/20 criteria; low risk observe, high risk consider trial or select systemic therapy

drugs.name: Lenalidomide (high-risk select-patient option only)

provenance.locator: MYEL-3 (Smoldering Myeloma, High risk, Select patients: Lenalidomide (category 2B)); MS-9 (single-agent lenalidomide improved PFS in high-risk smoldering myeloma)

drugs.notes: SURVEILLANCE IS PRIMARY. This drug entry represents the high-risk, select-patient systemic-therapy option only; it is NOT recommended for standard-risk smoldering myeloma. The guideline lists single-agent Lenalidomide as a category 2B option for high-risk smoldering myeloma (MYEL-3), supported by a randomized trial showing improved PFS (MS-9). Daratumumab is a category 1 select-patient option (AQUILA). NO smoldering-specific dose or schedule is printed in the provided source, so dosePerUnit is VERIFY and days is left empty pending a cited dose; do NOT infer a cytotoxic dose for smoldering disease. If used, lenalidomide requires VTE thromboprophylaxis and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen).

supportiveCare: Primary management is active surveillance (observation): low-risk observe at 3- to 6-month intervals (category 1); high-risk prefer enrollment in a clinical trial (strongly recommended) or observe at 3-month intervals.
Select high-risk patients only: Daratumumab (category 1; AQUILA) or Lenalidomide (category 2B) may be considered; doses are not established in the provided source (VERIFY).

Follow-up labs: CBC with differential and platelets; creatinine, albumin, corrected calcium, serum quantitative immunoglobulins, SPEP, SIFE; serum free light-chain assay; 24-hour urine (UPEP, UIFE) as needed.
Imaging: whole-body MRI without contrast, whole-body low-dose CT, and/or FDG-PET/CT annually or as clinically indicated, ideally with the same modality used at diagnosis.

monitoring: Serial monoclonal-protein and serum free light-chain trends (rising parameters indicate higher risk and closer monitoring)
CBC, renal function, corrected calcium (surveillance for evolution to symptomatic myeloma / CRAB features)
reassess risk over time (patients can evolve from low to high risk)

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 74 (Plasma Cell Neoplasms): smoldering (asymptomatic) myeloma defined by disease burden below symptomatic myeloma with no related organ/tissue impairment; historic management is observation

guideline.locator: MYEL-3 (Smoldering Myeloma: low risk observe 3-6 months category 1; high risk clinical trial preferred or observe, select patients Daratumumab category 1 / Lenalidomide category 2B); MS-9 (Primary Therapy for Smoldering Myeloma; AQUILA daratumumab; single-agent lenalidomide PFS benefit)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for smoldering (asymptomatic) myeloma (#83). Active surveillance (observation) is the primary management: low-risk patients observe at 3- to 6-month intervals (category 1); high-risk patients prefer enrollment in a clinical trial (strongly recommended) or observation at 3-month intervals, with Daratumumab (category 1; AQUILA) or single-agent Lenalidomide (category 2B) as select-patient systemic-therapy options. Risk is stratified by the Mayo 2018 / IMWG 20/2/20 criteria. Sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Multiple Myeloma v5.2026 (MYEL-3, MS-9) and DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 74. NO cytotoxic dose was invented for smoldering disease: the single drug entry represents the high-risk lenalidomide option, and because the provided source prints no smoldering-specific dose or schedule, dosePerUnit, regimen.cycleLengthDays and regimen.cycles are set to VERIFY (and treatmentIntent VERIFY, since the intent of early intervention is delay of progression rather than a clean curative/palliative label). These VERIFY fields are listed in verifyFields and keep the protocol at DRAFT. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
